---
title: "DSL Examples"
---

Each example below parses cleanly and runs against either the hardware controller or the PyBullet digital twin. Examples marked "legacy" use the original line-based format; the interpreter accepts both.

## 1. Minimal move

```
MOVE HOME_REST
```

The simplest valid sequence. The arm moves to the `HOME_REST` pose and the sequence terminates.

## 2. Timed carry demo (legacy format)

```
# META_FULL_DEMO: height + range + rotation + claw + drop + recover
HOME_REST 500
STOW_COMPACT 500

# descend and grab
LOW_APPROACH_OPEN 800
LOW_GRAB_CLOSE 500

# lift through multiple heights
LIFT_MID_CARRY 700
LIFT_HIGH_CARRY 800

# rotate and sweep
ROTATE_LEFT_SCAN 700
ROTATE_RIGHT_SCAN 700

# drop and recover
DROP_HIGH_OPEN 700
HOME_REST 700

REPEAT 3
```

`compat.py` rewrites this into an outer `REPEAT 3 { ... }` block before parsing.

## 3. Sensor-gated branch

```
IF TOF[0] < 250 {
  MOVE HOME_REST WAIT 100
} ELSE {
  MOVE STOW_COMPACT WAIT 100
}
```

If the front ToF channel sees a surface closer than 250 mm, retreat to `HOME_REST`; otherwise fold into `STOW_COMPACT`.

## 4. Define a pose and drive a joint

```
STATE MY_POSE {
  JOINTS 90 90 90 90 90 73
}

MOVE MY_POSE WAIT 250
SET B 45 WAIT 500
```

Definitions and statements interleave freely. `STATE` registrations take effect immediately, so a subsequent `MOVE` resolves against them.

## 5. Obstacle-aware sim program

```
OBSTACLE PILLAR {
  POS 150 0 80
  RADIUS 40
  SHAPE CYLINDER
}

REPEAT 5 {
  MOVE HOME_REST WAIT 200
  MOVE PICKUP_READY WAIT 400
}
```

`OBSTACLE` is ignored on the hardware backend; in the digital twin the planner sees the virtual pillar and routes around it.

## 6. Sensor-driven retreat loop

```
WHILE IR > 0 {
  MOVE STEP WAIT 50
}
```

The loop exits as soon as all IR sensors report clear. The 10 000-iteration safety cap prevents a hung sensor from stalling the arm indefinitely.

## 7. Conditional pickup with a joint read

```
MOVE APPROACH
WHILE JOINT[B] < 120 {
  SET B 100 WAIT 100
}
MOVE GRIP
```

The `WHILE JOINT[B] < 120` condition polls the actual servo position, not a cached target, so mid-loop resistance or safety refusals do not break the termination condition.
